source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
Fertilizer is organic and inorganic material used to nourish plants so they grow well. Growing crops year after year depletes soil fertility gradually, so to keep corn growing well, farmers need to replenish the soil with additional nutrient sources. Fertilizer timing is generally aligned with land preparation and topdressing. The specific fertilizer program for corn can vary depending on the existing soil fertility.

Organic/natural fertilizer: Applying organic (natural) fertilizer is of primary importance because it can improve soil quality over the long term and supply nutrients well over an extended period. In this context, farmers can use animal manure, compost, or various types of decomposed organic waste.

Chemical (mineral) fertilizer: Nitrogen, Phosphate, and Potassium (Potash) fertilizers are used.

Fertilizer application rate and method table:
- Organic/natural fertilizer: 10-15 tons/ha, applied 100% as basal (at planting), 0% at first topdressing (15 days) and 0% at second topdressing (30 days).
- Compound fertilizer (formulations such as 15-15-15, DAP, or 20-20-15): 200-300 kg/ha, applied 30% as basal, 35% at first topdressing (15 days after planting), and 35% at second topdressing (30 days after planting).
- Urea: 150 kg/ha, applied 0% as basal, 50% at first topdressing (15 days), and 50% at second topdressing (30 days).

Liquid/foliar topdressing fertilizer should be sprayed on day 13-14 and again on day 35-37 after planting.
